accepted.decision: Doctor keeps its current verdict surface (missingFiles, modifiedFiles, missingDiscovery, harnessProblems, ok, exit codes) and gains a second, non-failing dimension: five enforcement checks that answer "at what level is this claimed gate actually run", each returning {id, level, state, evidence}. The hard boundary is made structural rather than stated: all reading of the inspected repository happens in one module (`evidence.ts` and its readers), over a declared read set — the files `construct.json` records plus a fixed allowlist (package.json, the vitest/vite config, `.github/workflows/*.y(a)ml`, lefthook/husky/simple-git-hooks configs, `.git/config`) — with no recursive walk, no spawn, no dynamic import; the five checks are pure functions of those facts, so "doctor executes nothing" is auditable in one file and enforced by the repo's `spawnPolicy` lint block. Check ids are exactly `lint-policy`, `construct-tests`, `ci`, `hook`, `red-gate` — one per broken fixture, with `healthy` as the control that pins all five; typecheck stays out of the check set as a per-preset warning list (a framework matrix would grow faster than we close it), so the fixture-to-id enumeration stays total. The level chain is shared: a check is `present` when its artifact exists and the harness can reach it, and its level is L3 when a workflow runs the harness command, else L2 when a readable hook config runs it, else L0; absence of an artifact is `absent` at L0; anything doctor cannot read literally is `unknown`, never `absent`; L4 is never emitted because branch protection and rulesets are not in the repository. `weakestLink` is the lowest level among checks whose state is `present` (the gates the repository claims), ties broken by the canonical check order, null when nothing is claimed — absent and unknown checks are printed on their own lines but excluded, so a fresh construct that ships no hook reports L3 rather than a permanent L0 that people learn to ignore. `ok` remains `missingFiles.length === 0 && harnessProblems.length === 0`: the five broken fixtures still exit 0, and what flips in the table is what doctor now *says*, not the exit code. Alternatives rejected: resolving the target's eslint config (the supply-chain vector the whole task exists to close), running the harness to answer red-gate (same), walking the inspected tree for policy tests (unbounded read set, node_modules), and one flat doctor.ts (the file already outgrew a one-phrase responsibility).
accepted.contractChanges: This repository has no OpenAPI contract; doctor's boundary contract is `doctor --json`, and its source of truth is docs/cli.md. The change is additive only: `checks: Array<{ id: 'lint-policy' | 'construct-tests' | 'ci' | 'hook' | 'red-gate', level: 'L0'|'L1'|'L2'|'L3'|'L4', state: 'present'|'absent'|'unknown', evidence: string }>` ordered by the canonical CHECK_IDS order; `weakestLink: { id, level } | null`; `warnings: string[]` carrying the per-preset typecheck caveat (empty for presets with none). `ok`, `missingFiles`, `modifiedFiles`, `missingDiscovery` and `harnessProblems` keep their names, types and meaning, and stay first in the emitted object so existing consumers are untouched. The exported TypeScript surface of the command moves but does not change: `runDoctor`, `printDoctor`, `DoctorResult`, `DISCOVERY_PLACEHOLDER`, `isMarkerFilled`, `markerOpen`, `markerClose` are re-exported from `src/commands/doctor/index.ts`, with `CHECK_IDS`, `LEVELS`, `CheckId`, `Level`, `CheckState` and `CheckVerdict` added for the fixture enumeration test. docs/cli.md gets the new JSON example, the check table (id, what it reads, what it can conclude), the weakest-link line, and one paragraph stating that doctor executes nothing from the repository it inspects and therefore never reports L4 and always reports red-gate as unknown.
accepted.compositionChanges: architecture/composition/doctor.yaml: rewrite the description (runDoctor in `src/commands/doctor/index.ts` is the composition root; it reads construct.json, gathers file evidence once, fans out to five pure checks and the three existing verdicts, fans them into the report, and ends with one weakest-link line; it executes nothing from the repository it inspects and writes nothing). Boundaries: keep `entry`, `checks`, `report`; add `evidence` ("Evidence · file reads only"). Nodes: `cli` (src/cli.ts), `run` (src/commands/doctor/index.ts), `manifest` (src/manifest.ts), `files` → src/commands/doctor/baseline.ts, `markers` → src/commands/doctor/discovery.ts, `harness` → src/commands/doctor/harness.ts; new `evidence` node "construct.json files + package.json, vitest include globs, workflows, hook configs · read only" (src/commands/doctor/evidence.ts) in the evidence boundary; new check nodes in the checks boundary — `lintPolicy` (checks/lint-policy.ts), `constructTests` (checks/construct-tests.ts), `ci` (checks/ci.ts), `hook` (checks/hook.ts), `redGate` (checks/red-gate.ts); new `weakest` node "weakestLink · lowest level among the claimed gates" (src/commands/doctor/verdict.ts) and `print` repointed to src/commands/doctor/report.ts. Edges: cli→run (sequence); run→manifest (sequence); manifest→evidence (sequence); manifest fan-out to files, markers, harness; evidence fan-out to the five check nodes; the five checks fan-in to weakest; files, markers, harness and weakest fan-in to print. Every node `path` must exist (composition:check validates paths), then regenerate architecture/doctor.md with `pnpm composition:render` and hand-edit only the prose section below the markers, adding that levels and the weakest link never change the exit code.
constraints: Doctor executes nothing from the repository it inspects: no `node:child_process`, no `import()` of any path in it, no `require`/`createRequire`/`node:module`, no invocation of the target's eslint/vitest APIs. Every verdict is derived from reading file text.

The spawn policy must prove that constraint in this branch. `eslint.config.mjs`'s `spawnPolicy` block on `src/**` (ignoring only `src/detect/package-manager.ts`) currently restricts only the `node:child_process` import on `main`; if the base does not already carry them, add `ImportExpression`, `CallExpression[callee.name="require"]`, `MemberExpression[object.name="require"]`, `ImportDeclaration[source.value="node:module"]` and `Identifier[name="createRequire"]` with the same wording as branch `fix/spawn-policy-covers-dynamic-import`, keeping the block cumulative (antfu's `TSEnumDeclaration[const=true]` and `TSExportAssignment` restated), and extend tests/dependency-policy.test.ts with one lint sample per form.

Doctor's read set is declared and bounded: the files recorded in `construct.json` plus a named allowlist constant — `package.json`, `vitest.config.{ts,mts,js,mjs}` / `vite.config.*`, the entries of `.github/workflows/` (one readdir), `lefthook.{yml,yaml,toml,json}`, `.husky/*`, `.simple-git-hooks.*`, the `simple-git-hooks` key in package.json, `.git/config`. No recursive walk of the inspected tree, no path outside `root`, and every read guarded so a missing or unreadable file yields `unknown` instead of throwing.

All reads live in `src/commands/doctor/evidence.ts` and the readers it calls (`harness.ts`, `runner.ts`, `workflows.ts`, `hooks.ts`); the five checks under `src/commands/doctor/checks/` are pure functions of `(manifest, evidence)` returning a `CheckVerdict` and touch no filesystem, so they are testable without temp directories.

`src/commands/doctor/index.ts` is the only composition root: it reads the manifest, gathers evidence once, fans out to baseline / discovery / harness / the five checks, and fans the verdicts into `DoctorResult`. No check calls another check; the shared level chain lives in `enforcement.ts` and is called by the checks, not duplicated in them.

Exit semantics do not change: `ok = missingFiles.length === 0 && harnessProblems.length === 0`. Levels, states and the weakest link never influence `ok`, `printDoctor`'s return value, or the `--json` exit code, and a freshly initialised repository still exits 0.

`ci` returns only `present` or `unknown`, never `absent`; no check ever returns `L4`; `red-gate` is always `unknown` and its evidence states that doctor executes nothing and that CI is where a clean checkout is proven; a runner include that is missing, non-literal (a variable, a spread, a template literal or a call) yields `unknown`, never `absent`.

Level rules are shared and fixed: harness level is L3 when a `run:` step in a workflow invokes the harness command, else L2 when a readable hook config runs it, else L0. A check whose artifact is missing or unreachable by the harness is `absent` at L0; a check whose artifact exists and is reachable is `present` at the harness level; evidence always names the file or key read and, when the chain breaks, the weakest link.

`checks` is ordered by `CHECK_IDS` = ['lint-policy','construct-tests','ci','hook','red-gate']; `weakestLink` is the lowest level among checks whose state is `present`, ties broken by that order, `null` when no check is present. Exactly one weakest-link line is printed, as the last line, in both the themed and the plain report.

Framing strings (the checks heading, the weakest-link line, the nothing-is-claimed line, the typecheck caveat lead-in) go in `src/ui/lore.ts` with a `PLAIN_LORE` counterpart; computed facts (evidence strings, harness problems, per-preset caveat text) are built in the doctor modules exactly as today's `harnessProblems` strings are. `--plain` output carries no lore vocabulary and no emoji.

Typecheck is not a check and gets no id and no fixture: `src/commands/doctor/typecheck.ts` holds a per-preset caveat list (today one entry, `node-frontend`: a Vite app that adds `.vue`/`.svelte` single-file components needs the framework's own checker because `tsc --noEmit` does not see them), emitted as a `warnings` entry only when the manifest's preset is listed and the resolved harness text does not already name that checker.

No new dependency: glob matching for include globs, the workflow scan and the hook-config scan are literal text operations written in-repo (the CLI's runtime dependencies stay `@clack/prompts`, `citty`, `picocolors`).

The fixture table stays one table in tests/doctor-fixtures.test.ts keyed by fixture directory, each row naming `ok` plus the check id, level, state (and, where it matters, an evidence substring) that fixture provokes; the five broken fixtures keep their files byte-for-byte. Only `tests/fixtures/doctor/healthy/` changes, and only so the control genuinely holds every property: `test` becomes `vitest run`, the vitest include becomes `['tests/**/*.test.ts', 'scripts/tests/**/*.test.ts']` (mirroring templates/harness/vitest.config.ts), and `scripts/tests/lint/syntax-policy.test.ts` is added, calling `calculateConfigForFile` like the node-backend preset ships.

Artifacts first, in order: decision 0007 and its README row, the security-invariants row, then architecture/composition/doctor.yaml; then the code; then `pnpm composition:render`. architecture/doctor.md inside the `composition:doctor` markers is generated output and is never hand-edited (composition:check runs inside quality).

Public surface is preserved by re-export from `src/commands/doctor/index.ts`; update the three importers (`src/cli.ts`, `tests/init.test.ts`, `tests/doctor-fixtures.test.ts`) to `./commands/doctor/index.js` (NodeNext needs the explicit file), and extend `dependencyBoundary()` in eslint.config.mjs with the `../../<module>` forms so the `src/commands` rule still applies one directory deeper.

The check list is described in exactly one place, docs/cli.md. README.md keeps its one-line summary; AGENTS.md's composition-roots block and the CLAUDE.md layout row only get the path change `src/commands/doctor.ts` → `src/commands/doctor/`.

No comments anywhere in the new source including JSDoc; style is fixed with `pnpm lint:fix`; every new logic module ships its test in the same change; no existing test is weakened, skipped or deleted; add a changeset.

files: src/commands/doctor.ts (delete, split into the files below)

brief:
Task: Replace doctor's substring matching with an enforcement level, and give doctor a boundary it can defend.

Today `harnessProblems` in src/commands/doctor.ts looks for the substrings lint, typecheck and test inside the `quality` script and calls the harness intact when it finds them. On a real repository that produced OK while ESLint loaded a config that never saw the construct policy, the construct's own tests fell outside the runner's globs, and typecheck could not pass on that stack at all. Presence of a command is not a level of enforcement.

Every check now returns an id, a level from L0 to L4, a state of present, absent or unknown, and a short evidence string naming the file or key it read. The levels: L0 is text or a command nobody is obliged to run; L1 is a human in review; L2 is local, a hook, bypassable with --no-verify; L3 is CI that does not block a merge; L4 is CI that blocks a merge.

The hard constraint, from which the rest follows: DOCTOR EXECUTES NOTHING FROM THE REPOSITORY IT INSPECTS. No child process, no dynamic import of a path inside it, no createRequire into its node_modules. `doctor` is run through npx in a fresh clone — at exactly the moment a person has not yet decided whether they trust that code — and resolving the target's eslint.config.mjs means running that code on the instruction "check whether this repository is honest". A flat config is a module, so "we only read the config" is not a defence. This is the difference between a linter and a supply-chain vector. The repository's own spawn policy already forbids these forms under src/, so the constraint is enforced, not merely stated.

What each check may therefore conclude:

- lint: resolution belongs to the target's harness, not to doctor. The presets already ship a test that runs ESLint's calculateConfigForFile under the project's own vitest inside its own quality script. Doctor answers the level question only: does such a policy check exist in the repository, is its file inside the runner's include globs, is the runner invoked by the harness command, is the harness command invoked by a workflow. Report the level that chain supports and name the weakest link in the evidence.
- tests: the construct's tests are in the runner's include list, read literally from the config. A non-literal include — a glob built by a function call or a variable — yields unknown, never absent.
- CI: present or unknown, and never absent. Branch protection and organisation rulesets live in the GitHub API, not in files, so doctor has no complete scope evidence by construction. For the same reason doctor NEVER reports L4: the most a file can show is L3.
- hook: husky, lefthook, simple-git-hooks or a core.hooksPath setting in .git/config gives L2. A bare command in package.json scripts with none of those is L0.
- red gate: whether the harness command passes on a clean checkout requires running it, which doctor will not do, so this is always unknown in doctor and says so in its evidence. CI is where that is proven.
- typecheck: no general applicability detector. A per-preset warning list only, for the stacks where a bare tsc --noEmit cannot pass; a framework matrix grows faster than we close it.

The output ends with exactly one line naming the weakest link: the lowest level among the gates the repository claims. Honesty without a summary line becomes noise that people stop reading. The exit code semantics do not change — 1 for a missing baseline file or a broken harness, 0 otherwise — and in particular a freshly initialised repository must still exit 0, since the acceptance matrix runs doctor on one. A low weakest link is information, not a failure.

The six fixtures under tests/fixtures/doctor/ currently assert that doctor says ok true on five repositories that are objectively broken, each test naming the lie. Flip each of those rows to the specific id, level and state the new check reports, in the same commit that adds the check, so the diff reads as a behaviour change rather than as rewritten tests. Expectations stay in the one table keyed by fixture directory. The cross-check test that compares the table against the fixture directories now becomes what it was always meant to be: an enumeration of doctor's own check ids, failing when a check has no fixture.

src/commands/doctor.ts has outgrown a responsibility that can be named in one phrase — split it into src/commands/doctor/ with one file per concern and a composition root that fans out to the checks and fans the verdicts into the report, matching the existing shape of the codebase.

Artifacts to change before or with the code: a decision record numbered 0007 recording as ONE decision that doctor executes nothing from the repository it audits and therefore never claims L4, appended to architecture/decisions/README.md in number order; a row in architecture/security-invariants.md naming that constraint with the spawn policy block and its test as the enforcement, following the convention that the column names the mechanism and not a tool; architecture/composition/doctor.yaml updated for the new checks and the weakest-link line, then architecture/doctor.md regenerated with `pnpm composition:render` — composition:check runs inside quality, so a hand-edited rendered doc fails the gate; and docs/cli.md for the new --json shape and the weakest-link line.

The --json shape gains checks, an array of id, level, state and evidence, plus weakestLink, and keeps missingFiles, modifiedFiles, missingDiscovery and harnessProblems so that today's consumers keep working.

Repository conventions: no comments in source including JSDoc, every user-facing string lives in src/ui/lore.ts with its PLAIN_LORE counterpart and --plain output carries no lore and no emoji, tests live in tests/ and never beside source, style is fixed by running lint:fix rather than by hand, no dependency is added, and no existing test is weakened or skipped.

Acceptance criteria so far:
- Every check returns id, level in L0 to L4, state in present, absent or unknown, and evidence naming what it read; doctor --json carries checks and weakestLink alongside the existing missingFiles, modifiedFiles, missingDiscovery and harnessProblems fields, and plain output ends with exactly one weakest-link line naming the lowest level among the claimed gates.
- Each of the five broken fixtures flips from ok true to the specific id, level and state its check reports, in the same commit that adds that check, with the expectations still in one table keyed by the fixture directory; the healthy control still reports a healthy construct, and the cross-check now enumerates doctor's check ids and fails when a check has no fixture.
- Doctor never spawns a process, dynamically imports a path inside the inspected repository or reaches its node_modules — the repository's own spawn policy proves this by failing the build otherwise — the CI check returns present or unknown and never absent and never L4, the red-gate check is always unknown with evidence saying why, and a non-literal runner include yields unknown rather than absent.
- Hook detection returns L2 for each of husky, lefthook, simple-git-hooks and a core.hooksPath setting, and L0 for a bare script with none of them; exit codes are unchanged and a freshly initialised repository still exits 0 from doctor --plain.
- Decision 0007 records doctor executing nothing and never claiming L4 as one decision and is listed in architecture/decisions/README.md; architecture/security-invariants.md carries the matching row naming the mechanism; architecture/composition/doctor.yaml is updated and architecture/doctor.md regenerated so composition:check passes; docs/cli.md describes the new output; pnpm run quality is green.

The task is classified as high effort; design it before any implementation.
